problem: The definition says 'a nonzero integer a'. A nonzero multiple of p, such as a=p, satisfies x²≡a (mod p) with x=0, so the wording would call it a quadratic residue. But the Legendre symbol is 0 when p divides a, and standard definitions exclude p|a from being a nonzero quadratic residue. Quiz Q1 repeats the same wording.
fix: Say 'a nonzero residue class modulo p' or 'an integer a with p∤a'. In Q1, state that a is a quadratic residue modulo p when p∤a and x²≡a (mod p) has a solution.

problem: The sentence 'The squares of 1, 2, …, p−1 produce every residue' is false. They produce only the quadratic residues, and only (p−1)/2 distinct nonzero values. A student may read 'every residue' literally.
fix: Say 'The squares of 1, 2, …, p−1 produce every quadratic residue modulo p, each nonzero square twice.'

problem: The question asks why there are exactly (p−1)/2 'nonzero residues modulo p'. Literally there are p−1 nonzero residue classes modulo p. The intended phrase is 'nonzero quadratic residues'.
fix: Rewrite Q2 as: 'Why are there exactly (p−1)/2 nonzero quadratic residues modulo p?'

problem: Quadratic reciprocity is stated for 'two odd primes p and q' without requiring them to be distinct. If p=q, the left side contains (p/p)=0 and the formula is false. Standard statements require distinct odd primes.
fix: Add 'distinct' in both places: 'distinct odd primes p and q'.

problem: The text says 'Supplement rules handle −1 and 2' but never gives those rules, so the student cannot compute Jacobi symbols involving −1 or 2 from this chapter alone.
fix: State the supplement rules: (−1/n)=(-1)^((n−1)/2) and (2/n)=(-1)^((n²−1)/8) for odd n.
